notes: Every fixture is a working script carrying the defects the skill covers on the exact lines the request forces the agent to touch: no strict mode, unquoted expansions, a predictable temp path with no cleanup, eval on a caller-supplied name, a hand-built JSON payload, a password in argv generated from $RANDOM, and a traversal over `$(ls)`.
No prompt mentions security, hardening, quoting, or shellcheck. Each one is an ordinary feature request, so only the skill can surface the rest.

The fixtures ship no .shellcheckrc. Default ShellCheck already reports the unquoted expansions, so a pass on the quoting assertions measures whether the agent ran the linter at all; the strict-mode, cleanup, validation, and secret assertions are the ones no linter answers.
bss-01 and bss-04 are runnable inside the workspace against their own sample data. bss-02 and bss-03 call ssh, curl, useradd and mysql, so they are graded statically plus `bash -n`.

tasks.title: Extend a log archiving script with multi-service and retention support
tasks.prompt: bin/archive-logs.sh handles one service per run and archives are pruned by hand. Extend it so several service names can be given in a single invocation, add a --keep-days N option that removes archives older than N days once the new archives are in place, and make it print a one-line summary of what was archived. Update the README to describe the new usage.

tasks.title: Add a release note and a dry-run mode to a deploy notifier
tasks.prompt: The person deploying should be able to add a short release note that appears in the Slack message, passed as a third argument to bin/notify-deploy.sh. Add that, and add a --dry-run flag that prints what the script would do instead of restarting the service or posting the message. Document both in the README.

tasks.title: Batch account provisioning from a file
tasks.prompt: Provisioning runs one account at a time today. Add a --from-file option to sbin/provision-user.sh that reads account names from a file, one per line, and a --shell option that sets the login shell for the accounts it creates. Print a summary line for each account it provisions. Update the README.

tasks.title: Parameterize a cleanup script and add a dry-run mode
tasks.prompt: bin/clean-workspaces.sh hardcodes the workspace root and the age threshold, so every CI worker needs its own copy of it. Take both as arguments, keeping the current values as defaults, and add a --dry-run mode that lists what would be removed without removing anything. Update the README.
